Based on all my experiments, I can now describe the function:

The function implements ROT13 cipher, which rotates alphabetic characters by 13 positions (a↔n, b↔o, etc.), preserving case. Non-alphabetic characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) are left unchanged. ROT13 is its own inverse, so applying it twice returns the original.

[DESCRIPTION]: The function implements the ROT13 cipher. It takes a string input and rotates each alphabetic character by 13 positions in the alphabet (wrapping around at z/Z). Lowercase letters map within lowercase (a→n, n→a), and uppercase letters map within uppercase (A→N, N→A). Non-alphabetic characters (digits, spaces, punctuation, symbols) are preserved unchanged. Since ROT13 is an involution, applying the function twice restores the original text.

[CODE]:
```python
def f(x):
    result = []
    for ch in x:
        if 'a' <= ch <= 'z':
            result.append(chr((ord(ch) - ord('a') + 13) % 26 + ord('a')))
        elif 'A' <= ch <= 'Z':
            result.append(chr((ord(ch) - ord('A') + 13) % 26 + ord('A')))
        else:
            result.append(ch)
    return ''.join(result)
```
